content.value_statement: Graph analysis often requires many algorithms, formats, and visualization choices. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical NetworkX workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates undirected, directed, multigraph, and multidigraph structures with node and edge attributes.
Explains shortest paths, centrality, clustering, connectivity, matching, flow, and community detection algorithms.
Generates classic, random, lattice, tree, social, and degree-sequence graph models.
Covers graph import and export using edge lists, GraphML, JSON, CSV, matrices, SQLite, DOT, and compressed files.
Guides static and interactive network visualization with layouts, labels, styling, Plotly, PyVis, and publication exports.
Provides performance guidance for large graphs, sparse matrices, compressed formats, and approximate algorithms.
limitations: It is reference guidance and does not execute NetworkX code by itself.
Large graph performance still depends on memory, graph density, and chosen algorithms.
Some visualization and Graphviz workflows require optional Python packages or system tools.
Results from random generators and layouts require fixed seeds for reproducibility.

use_cases.title: Map Research Relationships
use_cases.description: Build citation, collaboration, or knowledge graphs and calculate centrality, paths, clusters, and communities.

use_cases.title: Analyze Product Networks
use_cases.description: Model users, items, events, or dependencies as graphs and find influential nodes or weak links.

use_cases.title: Prototype Graph Features
use_cases.description: Design Python workflows for loading graph data, testing algorithms, exporting results, and preparing visual outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Use NetworkX to create a graph from these entities and relationships. Explain the graph type, node attributes, edge attributes, and basic checks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Graph Algorithms
prompt_templates.prompt: Given my graph goal and data shape, recommend NetworkX algorithms for paths, centrality, clustering, and communities. Include assumptions and expected outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Import and Export Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a NetworkX workflow to read my graph data, validate it, compute metrics, and export results. Compare suitable file formats.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Large Network Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this NetworkX analysis plan for a large graph. Suggest faster algorithms, sparse representations, sampling choices, and visualization limits.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to analyze a small social network.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends an undirected graph, degree and betweenness centrality, connected components, community detection, and a labeled spring layout.

output_examples.input: A user needs to exchange graph data with another tool.
output_examples.output: The skill compares edge lists, GraphML, JSON node-link data, CSV tables, DOT, and SQLite for the user's workflow.

output_examples.input: A user has a large sparse network with slow analysis.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests sparse matrix conversion, approximate centrality, compressed formats, subgraph loading, and reproducible random seeds.

best_practices: Choose the graph type before loading data, especially for directed or repeated edges.
Validate node counts, edge counts, connectivity, and attributes before running expensive algorithms.
Use fixed random seeds for layouts, random graph generators, and sampled approximations.
anti_patterns: Do not use dense matrix methods for large sparse graphs without checking memory needs.
Do not compare centrality scores across different graph projections without documenting assumptions.
Do not export private relationship data without reviewing the target format and destination.

faq.question: What is NetworkX best for?
faq.answer: It is best for Python graph modeling, algorithm exploration, graph metrics, and small to medium network analysis.

faq.question: Can this skill handle directed graphs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers directed graphs, multidirected graphs, directed paths, strong components, and directed generators.

faq.question: Does it create visualizations?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains static matplotlib plots, layout choices, styling, interactive views, and export formats.

faq.question: Can it read existing graph files?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers edge lists, adjacency lists, GraphML, GML, JSON, CSV, matrices, SQLite, and DOT.

faq.question: Is NetworkX suitable for very large graphs?
faq.answer: Sometimes. Large graphs may need sparse structures, approximations, sampling, or specialized graph systems.

faq.question: Does the skill run code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The user or agent must choose when to execute code.
